title: feat: autotune dynamic MXFP8 layout and TRTLLM tactic
body:
## Description

Add `mm_mxfp8_dynamic_quant`, a TRTLLM-backed API that profiles BF16 activation quantization and MXFP8 GEMM as one operation. The autotuner jointly selects the activation scale layout (`8x4` or `128x4`) and a valid TRTLLM tactic for each `(M, N, K)` bucket, then reuses that choice from the normal FlashInfer autotune cache.

This does not add a new GEMM kernel. It connects the existing MXFP8 quantizer, TRTLLM layouts, tactic enumeration, and autotuner so serving can choose the fastest valid combination for the observed shape. One composite tactic `(layout, tactic_id)` is cached per profile.

`prepare_mxfp8_trtllm_weights` provides the matching public weight-preparation path, including padded scale storage for `N` values divisible by 32 but not 128. The existing fixed-layout API and its tuning buckets are unchanged.

## How the layout is selected

There is no fixed `M` threshold. For each `(M, N, K)` optimization profile, the runner enumerates the cross product of both activation-scale layouts and every valid TRTLLM tactic:

```text
(8x4, tactic 0..A) + (128x4, tactic 0..B)
                 -> profile quantization + GEMM
                 -> cache the fastest (layout, tactic_id)
```

The selected pair is reused from the normal FlashInfer autotune cache. A cache miss keeps the existing 8x4 fallback.

The measured shapes show a clear trend, but also show why a shape-aware choice is needed:

| M range | Faster fixed layout in this sweep |
|---|---|
| `M <= 128` | 8x4 for 40/40 shapes |
| `M = 256` | mixed: 8x4 for 2/5, 128x4 for 3/5 |
| `M = 512` | mixed: 8x4 for 1/5, 128x4 for 4/5 |
| `M >= 1024` | 128x4 for 25/25 shapes |

Larger `N` moved the crossover earlier in the measured set: `N=8192/8832` crossed between `M=128` and `256`, while `N=2304` crossed between `M=512` and `1024`. These are observations, not dispatch rules; the autotuner still measures the full composite candidate set.

## Results

Measured on GB200 with CUDA Graph enabled. Every row includes BF16-to-MXFP8 activation quantization and MXFP8 GEMM. The sweep covers 75 representative dense-GEMM shapes and four repeated processes.

| Comparison | Geomean throughput change |
|---|---:|
| Adaptive vs fixed TRTLLM 8x4 | **+21.9%** |
| Adaptive vs fixed TRTLLM 128x4 | **+27.1%** |
| Adaptive vs best fixed TRTLLM layout per shape | **-0.34%** |
| Adaptive vs CuTeDSL 128x4 | **-9.8%** |

The faster fixed layout changes with shape: 8x4 won 43 of 75 shapes and 128x4 won 32. The adaptive cache selected both layouts and landed within 0.34% of a per-shape best-layout oracle. The CuTeDSL result is included as a boundary: this PR improves TRTLLM selection but does not change FlashInfer's automatic backend preference.

Layout selection was identical across four processes for 74 of 75 shapes. The one outlier was `(M,N,K)=(128,8832,8192)`: fixed 8x4 was 30.8% faster, but the autotuner selected 128x4 in three runs. This shape is called out for a follow-up exhaustive tactic-regret audit rather than being hidden by the aggregate geomean.

## Tests

- CPU-testable API, bucket, trace, benchmark-argument, and byte-accounting tests
- GB200 BF16-reference correctness for low-M and bucket-boundary shapes
- Both layout candidates in one composite tactic list
- Persistent autotune cache save/load replay
- Multi-GPU device selection and restoration
- CUDA Graph capture and replay after autotune warmup

Feature-head GB200 results before the latest-main merge: `35 passed` for GEMM and benchmark tests, plus `1 passed` for trace generation. The performance sweep produced all 1,200 expected rows (75 shapes, four modes, four processes).

## Related work

- #2653 added the TRTLLM dense MXFP8 backend and both scale layouts.
- #2554 and #3367 provide persistent autotune caches and runner-specific cache keys.
- #4684 separately updates the existing fixed-layout `mm_mxfp8` tuning objective. This PR adds a new dynamic-quantization API and does not depend on #4684.

`mypy` reports three existing `flashinfer/__init__.py` optional-export errors
(`msa_ops`, `mamba`, and `trace_apply`). The same errors reproduce on the pinned
upstream `main` commit with this PR absent.

### Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] Targeted CPU and GB200 tests passed on the feature implementation before the latest-main merge.
- [ ] Authorized GPU CI on the current merge head (requested; awaiting maintainer authorization).

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and benchmark setup. I reviewed the complete diff and test output.

## Reviewer Notes

Please focus on the public weight-preparation contract, composite layout/tactic caching, and the CUDA Graph warmup requirement.
